```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

**Upload Raw Data**

```{r}

bg <- as.data.frame(read_csv("../data/background-clean.csv"))
class <- as.data.frame(read_csv("../data/class-summary.csv"))
interest <- as.data.frame(read_csv("../data/interest-clean.csv"))
response_time <- as.data.frame(read_csv("../data/response-timing.csv"))
meta_data <- as.data.frame(read_csv("../data/survey-metadata.csv"))

head(bg)

```

**EDA**

```{r}

# prof (char) vs comf (double)

# programming 
prog_dist <- bg |>
  group_by(prog.prof) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(prog.comf),
            median = median(prog.comf),
            count = n()) |>
  ungroup()

prog_dist

# math 

math_dist <- bg |>
  group_by(math.prof) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(math.comf),
            median = median(math.comf),
            count = n()) |>
  ungroup()

math 

# stats 

stats_dist <- bg |>
  group_by(stat.prof) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(stat.comf),
            median = median(stat.comf),
            count = n()) |>
  ungroup()

stats_dist

# combine all 3 statistics into one table 
combined <- bg |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(prog.prof, math.prof, stat.prof,
             prog.comf, math.comf, stat.comf),
             names_to = c("subject", ".value"),
             names_pattern = "(prog|math|stat)\\.(prof|comf)") |>
  group_by(subject, prof) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(comf, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(comf, na.rm = TRUE),
            count = n(),
            .groups = "drop")

combined

```
**Visuals**

Bar Plot:
```{r}

ggplot(combined, aes(x = subject, y = mean, fill = prof)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Comfortability by Subject and Proficiency",
    x = "Subject",
    y = "Mean Comfortability",
    fill = "Proficiency") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#89CFEF", "#7285A5", "#1C2951"))
  theme_minimal()

```

Other visuals: 
```{r}

# violin plot
# mean comfortability based on subject
ggplot(combined, aes(x=subject, y = mean)) + 
  geom_violin(fill = "lightblue") + 
  labs(title = "Mean Comfortability by Subject",
       x = "Subject",
       y = "Mean Comfortability")

# boxplot 
ggplot(combined, aes(x=subject, y = mean)) + 
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") + 
  labs(title = "Mean Comfortability by Subject",
       x = "Subject",
       y = "Mean Comfortability")

```
In both visuals above, I am exploring the mean comfortability score by by each subject. Taken from the combined statistics above, these plots show the similarities between the math and stats comfortability score, while there is much more variability for programming, ranging lower between 3.0-4.25. As for math and stats, we can see the range falls more between 3.5-4.5.  

**Inferences:** (for sou ^)

-   In every subject, students who rate themselves more proficient also report higher comfort.
